title: Thresholdless Pager Stabilizer: probabilistic dedupe, temporal smoothing, and automated partial-evacuate runbook
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: recurring noisy pager churn during transient SLO degradations in a single region causes on-call fatigue and increases time-to-resolution. Existing static thresholds generate duplicate pages across related signals (ingest errors, queue saturation, increased p95 latency), and current failover is an all-or-none region cutover which is costly and often unnecessary.

Goal: implement a 'thresholdless' stabilizer that reduces noise without delaying detection of real incidents. Components: 1) probabilistic deduplication model to collapse correlated events into a single actionable page, 2) temporal smoothing (adaptive smoothing window by SLO tier) to avoid oscillation, 3) SLO-tiered attenuation (different suppression aggressiveness for P99/P95-sensitive services), 4) automated partial-region quarantine (progressive traffic evacuation + controlled load shedding) with circuit-breaker hooks, 5) on-call playbook automation that guides responders and, where safe, remediates automatically (e.g., scale-up warm pools, enable caching bypass for critical paths).
acceptance_criteria: Reduce duplicate pager deliveries (same incident cluster) by >= 70% in the experimental region within 30 days
Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for true incidents does not increase by more than 10% after rollout
Partial-region quarantine can be executed automatically and rebalanced back within 30 minutes without data loss in >95% of tests
New dedupe + smoothing logic has unit and integration tests and is covered by a chaos experiment in staging
Runbook automation includes clear operator prompts, safe rollbacks, and post-incident telemetry links
tasks: Design probabilistic dedupe model: features, sampling strategy, training dataset (logs/alert fingerprints)
Prototype temporal smoother: implement adaptive window (30s-5min) that scales with SLO tier and signal volatility
Integrate suppression into alert-routing: policy layer to emit a single incident with summarized signals
Implement circuit-breaker hooks: open if region error-rate > 5x baseline AND p95 latency > 2x SLO for 3 min
Build partial-region quarantine operator: traffic weight shift API + automated 10%/min evacuation plan
Add automated load-shedding profiles: degrade non-critical features (vector-search fallback, throttle background jobs) during quarantine
Author on-call runbook flow and UI prompts in Console: guided checklist, rollback, telemetry links
Add e2e tests and chaos experiments in staging: simulate SLO blips and verify attenuation and evacuation behavior
Create Grafana dashboard and alert-quality metric (duplicate-pages, suppressed-pages, MTTA)
implementation_notes: Probabilistic dedupe: start with a lightweight logistic-regression model (features: alert fingerprint, fingerprint distance, time delta, host/region correlation, request bucket) trained on last 90 days of incidents. Threshold to emit single page set at predicted 'actionable' probability > 0.65

Temporal smoothing: smoothing_window = clip(90s * volatility_factor, 30s, 300s) where volatility_factor derived from rolling 10m signal variance. Higher SLO tier -> smaller window to prioritize low-latency alerts for critical endpoints
SLO-tier attenuation: P0 services receive minimal attenuation; P1/P2 eligible for stronger suppression during short lived spikes. Use labels on the service registry to pick attenuation profile
Circuit breaker criteria: combine error-rate (5x baseline) AND backlog growth OR sustained p95>2x for 3 minutes. Opening the breaker triggers partial-quarantine automation instead of full failover

Partial-region quarantine: iterative shift of 10% traffic per minute up to 70% with health probes gating each step. If downstream capacity drops or error rate increases, perform rollback to last healthy weight

Load shedding plan: tiered policies that first shed non-critical (batch/analytics) traffic, then degrade optional model features (e.g. lower-quality quantized models for non-critical routes), finally limit request rate per token for public endpoints if needed
Automation safety: every automatic action emits a high-priority incident with 'auto-action' tag and creates a read/write lock on the target routing policy so human operators can take control
Observability: add telemetry for suppression decisions (why suppressed, model score), evacuation progress, rollback events, and operator overrides
runbook_excerpt: Trigger: Alert cluster identified in region-us-west-2 with dedupe score >0.7 and >3 distinct signals (ingest_errors, kv-cache-miss, p95-latency)

Step 1 (automated): Evaluate circuit-breaker conditions. If met, attempt automated partial-region quarantine (10%/min up to 70%) with health-probes. Notify on-call with summary and one-click cancel/rollback

Step 2 (on-call): Confirm telemetry links: region overview, top offending services, recent deploys. If evacuation successful and errors drop, follow 'stabilize' checklist and plan gradual restore over 2 hours
Step 3 (automated remediation): Scale warm-pool capacity and enable caching bypass for critical paths. If auto-remediation fails twice, escalate to Runbook Owner
Step 4 (manual): If automation disabled or ineffective, follow manual partial-evacuate steps: adjust routing weights via Console, monitor error-rate and latency for each 10% step
Step 5 (post-incident): Run the 'pager-quality' report and tag false-positive root causes; feed back fingerprints into dedupe model training data
test_plan: Nightly chaos experiments in staging: induce 2m and 8m transient SLO degradations and verify suppression vs page generation
Load test partial-region quarantine with synthetic traffic to validate evacuation speed and graceful degradation
A/B rollout: enable stabilizer for 10% of traffic in us-west-2 for 2 weeks, compare duplicate-pager metric and MTTA against control
Runbook dry-runs with on-call squad: scheduled drills to exercise cancel/rollback and manual evacuation

notes: Rollout strategy: canary -> regional A/B -> global. Start with low-impact read-only services before enabling for core inference lanes
Keep an explicit 'auto-action' audit trail in the incident to comply with enterprise compliance requests
If model-based dedupe introduces missed-action risk, fall back to a deterministic rule-based suppressor at higher sensitivity
